title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
author: Daniel Huang, Qi He, Shaoxiong Duan, Yingjie Li et al.

summary: Streaming speech recognition is increasingly consumed by machines, such as translators and voice agents, that act on each token as it appears. A token that is later revised costs wasted work or a wrong action.
takeaways: Learning from LSP labels converts a full-context model into a stable-prefix streaming one without any architectural change.
Extensive evaluations show that R2T2 brings streaming recognition close to the base model's full-context quality while delivering stable text with low emission lag.

In this work, we present Confucius4-R2T2 (short for Real Real-Time Transcription), a stable-prefix streaming ASR model that never modifies its earlier output while maintaining high accuracy and low latency.
